papers.title: Genuinely Out-of-Equilibrium Bose-Einstein Condensation
papers.abstract: Bose-Einstein (BE) condensation typically occurs in the ground state. Prominent exceptions include excitons, whose ground state is the vacuum; consequently, they undergo BE condensation only in out-of-equilibrium regimes to counteract rapid decay. Here, we develop a driven-dissipative framework to address this challenge, demonstrating that BE condensates emerge under sufficiently strong excitation in one and two dimensions. In three dimensions, by incorporating effective loss rates and a specified injection energy, we find a percent-level condensate fraction, consistent in order of magnitude with the exciton experiment of Morita et al. (Nat. Commun. 13, 5388 (2022)).

papers.title: Determining quantum phases of eight-fold quasicrystal optical lattices with angular structure factor
papers.abstract: Quasicrystals have unique geometrical properties and are potential candidates to explore exotic states of matter. In this work, we explore the properties and the rotational symmetries of the quantum phases of ultracold atoms in the Ammann-Beenker quasicrystal optical lattice. We model the system with the quasicrystalline extended Bose-Hubbard model (qeBHM) and use mean field methods to identify the groundstate of qeBHM in the soft-core regime. To examine the diagonal long-range order of the groundstate quantum phases we develop a theoretical method to calculate the structure factor of the state. Our method clearly distinguishes various density wave (DW) and supersolid (SS) phases of the quasicrystal.

papers.title: Are superfluidity and superconductivity related to the spontaneous breaking of $U(1)$ symmetry?
papers.abstract: It is widely believed that superfluidity and superconductivity are caused by the spontaneous breaking of global $U(1)$ symmetry. We investigate this question for quantum-mechanical systems using the following precise criterion for spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB): the system's Hamiltonian and boundary conditions are invariant under transformations of a certain symmetry group, while the ground state is not. Through a simple analysis, we show that in real-world systems, which are always finite, spontaneous breaking of $U(1)$ symmetry does not occur. Therefore, superfluidity and superconductivity can be related to SSB only in infinite systems, which do not exist in our Universe. We also discuss the relationship between the theory of SSB and reality.

papers.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
papers.abstract: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.

papers.title: Phase diagram of the attractive lattice Fermi polaron and the instability of Nagaoka ferromagnetism
papers.abstract: On the square lattice, the attractive polaron competes not only with the dimeron but also with Yang's $\eta$ dimer, an exact eigenstate that maps onto the Nagaoka ferromagnet. With two-particle--hole Ans\"atze benchmarked by diagrammatic Monte Carlo, we find that the ground state evolves from polaron to dimeron to $\eta$ dimer at low filling, and, beyond a triple point, directly from polaron to $\eta$ dimer. Above 25\% filling it stays a polaron. As the $\eta$ dimer is exact, its boundary is a rigorous instability criterion for Nagaoka ferromagnetism, sharper than the previous best and logarithmic at low filling.

papers.title: Emergent Kinetic Constraints and Subspace Fragmentation in Rydberg Arrays
papers.abstract: In a strongly interacting Rydberg atom array, the dynamics are often constrained to the decoupled and fragmented Hilbert subspaces, representing an intriguing paradigm for nonergodicity. Here we investigate the Hilbert-space fragmentation in the degenerate subspaces arising from the interplay between tunable detuning and arbitrary long-range interactions in a one-dimensional Rydberg-atom array with lattice-translation symmetry. We analytically establish the conditions for the emergence of subspaces and their subsidiary fragmentations in the thermodynamic limit, enumerate the emergent kinetic constraints at the discrete dynamical points where dynamics are possible at all, and demonstrate the conditions for strong fragmentation and the rich scaling behaviors of the fragments. Our results provide systematic and analytical understandings of Hilbert-space fragmentation in Rydberg arrays, and shed light on engineering nonergodic many-body dynamics beyond the PXP model.

papers.title: Universal critical behavior in ideal Bose-Einstein condensation
papers.abstract: The experimental realization of photonic Bose-Einstein condensates has renewed the interest in the critical behavior of the ideal Bose gas, a paradigmatic system generally considered to be well understood. Here we establish a universal thermodynamic classification of ideal Bose-Einstein condensation in terms of experimentally measurable critical observables. We identify three universality classes with distinct critical exponents and singular thermodynamic behavior, arising from the low-energy scaling of the single-particle density of states. Depending on the low-energy scaling exponent of the density of states, which is controlled by dimensionality and confinement, the transition displays either the usual algebraic divergences of thermodynamic susceptibilities, divergent behavior with marginal logarithmic corrections, or a more subtle form of criticality, where only the correlation length diverges. Our work provides a unified framework for equilibrium criticality in noninteracting bosonic systems. This classification applies broadly to atomic, photonic, polaritonic, and magnonic condensates, where dimensionality, confinement, and spectral engineering can strongly reshape the density of states. We connect our thermodynamic classification with previously identified universality classes based on condensate fluctuations and order parameters.

papers.title: Phonon Scharnhorst effect: Acoustic analogue of the vacuum-fluctuation-boosted speed of light
papers.abstract: The Scharnhorst effect in quantum electrodynamics predicts a superluminal velocity shift $\delta c>0$ at low photon frequencies due to vacuum fluctuations between two mirrors. Although theoretically robust (no causality violation), the effect is extraordinarily small ($\delta c/c\approx 10^{-32}$ for mirrors $1\,\mu{\rm m}$ apart) and outside current experimental reach. Here we propose a condensed matter analogue, replacing the photons in the electromagnetic vacuum by phonon excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate. In an idealized geometry, the two-dimensional surface of a cylinder (circumference $L$) at zero temperature, the axial speed of sound is increased due to zero-point fluctuations of the condensate by $\delta c/c\simeq 5\times 10^{-3}\,\tilde{g}$ at $L\simeq 2\,\xi$, to first order in the dimensionless interaction constant $\tilde{g}\simeq 10^{-1}$ of the Bose gas of healing length $\xi\simeq 1\,\mu{\rm m}$. This is 28 orders of magnitude larger than the photonic effect at a comparable confinement length, basically because phonons have a self-interaction while photons only interact via massive electrons. When $L$ drops below $1.19\,\xi$ the velocity shift changes sign, signaling the crossover to a one-dimensional Bose gas. We discuss the prospects for observation of the acoustic Scharnhorst effect. The main obstacles are the nK temperature requirement and the need to separate the vacuum-fluctuation shift from a mean-field geometric correction.

papers.title: Spontaneous breaking of continuous scale invariance and Efimovian-like dynamics in a driven-dissipative system
papers.abstract: The Efimov effect manifests discrete scale invariance through a geometric series of three-body bound states. Analogous discrete scale symmetry has been observed in the Efimovian expansion of scale-invariant strongly interacting Fermi gases. However, it is unclear whether strong correlation is necessary. Here we investigate the spontaneous breaking of continuous scale invariance in a driven-dissipative two-level system whose driving and dissipation parameters scale as \(1/t\). By transforming to logarithmic time, we show that the evolution is governed by a non-Hermitian superoperator whose spectral decomposition reveals the emergence of a pair of eigenmodes with opposite real parts and equal imaginary parts. This signals the spontaneous breaking of continuous scale invariance and gives rise to Efimovian-like oscillations: log-periodic decay oscillations obeying discrete scaling laws. The onset of oscillations coincides with a PT-like-symmetry breaking transition in logarithmic time. Our work implies that the spontaneous breaking of continuous temporal scale symmetry and the emergence of Efimovian-like dynamics can be observed in a minimal driven-dissipative system without requiring strong correlations.

papers.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
papers.abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.
